cautions: T3 CRITICAL: Shao's tau (7.894 s) is the LIMITING lag between 1 keV and infinity - it is NOT the same quantity as Lu+2018's tau31 (0.66 s). Diffing them directly is a manufactured discrepancy.
omega is a limiting RMS HALF-width at 1 keV, not FWHM.
His pulses are fitted with a GAUSSIAN, not a FRED - the paper says asymmetric functions 'none of them worked perfectly'. Any pulse-shape diff must respect this.

published_disagreements_for_P3: SPECTRAL-EVOLUTION CLASS: Lu+2018 Table 4 says H (pure hard-to-soft); Yu+2019 Table 1 says 'h.t.s. to s.t.h.'; Shao+2017 Sec 4 argues both labels are ill-posed because Delta_tHR = 0.991 +- 0.101 s != 0. Three papers, three positions, one single-pulse burst.

DOES Ep TRACK FLUX: Yu+2019 measure F-Ep Spearman r = -0.25 (no tracking), yet the catalog flux peaks at +4.99 s and their Ep peaks in 3.60-4.71 s. The weak r is driven by low-S bins; an S>=20-only recomputation is OURS to do.

BEST MODEL: the GBM catalog prefers Comptonized (CPL) for BOTH the fluence and the peak-flux spectrum, with Band's beta unconstrained (-2.894 +- 4.431). GCN 12449 and Lu+2018 fit Band by default and never test CPL. Yu+2019 fit both but the DIC convention is unverified (T8).
multi_instrument_consensus_note: Phase 4 consensus procedure NOT applicable: only one instrument (Fermi/GBM) ever published a spectrum. INTEGRAL/SPI-ACS detected the burst (GCN 12449) but published nothing, so there is no inter-instrument spread to fold into an uncertainty. The Ep spread that DOES exist (GCN 692.5 / catalog Band 580.5 / catalog Comp 594.2 keV) is intra-instrument and interval-driven, not a systematic to inflate.
